name: Content Reporting
description: Tracks node page views, clicks, time-spent and GDPR consent, then reports and exports the aggregates on an admin dashboard.

suggests.drupal/eu_cookie_compliance: Provides the GDPR-consent signal read by the tracker's JS.
suggests.drupal/charts: Required by the content_reporting_charts submodule to render the graphs.

project_description: Content Reporting is a lightweight, self-contained analytics module for Drupal 9/10/11 that records how visitors engage with nodes and surfaces the results in an admin dashboard. A JavaScript behaviour attached to every node page POSTs a view event (and, when enabled, click and time-spent interaction events, plus a GDPR-consent flag read from the EU Cookie Compliance module) to backend endpoints. To keep page requests cheap, events are pushed onto Drupal core queues (content_reporting_track_queue and content_reporting_interactions_queue) and written to two custom tables (content_reporting_reports and content_reporting_interactions) by queue workers on cron. The dashboard at /admin/content-reporting/dashboard renders a paged, filterable table of per-node views, click breakdowns, time spent and GDPR-consent counts, and offers a CSV export. A settings form toggles the four tracking modes (GDPR, clicks, time-spent, logged-in users). A hook_cron purges report rows older than 30 days. The optional content_reporting_charts submodule adds a charts dashboard built on the contrib Charts module, rendering views-per-page, average time-spent per user type and average time-spent per page as column, bar and pie charts. The project is maintained for Drupal 10+ and is not covered by the security advisory policy.
